reasoning: This is a standard AUR -bin package with pinned upstream sources (GitHub releases), SHA-256 checksums for all downloaded artifacts, and a minimal package() function that only installs the prebuilt binary and documentation. No executable code runs during makepkg sourcing, no network operations occur outside of fetching pinned upstream artifacts, and no injection patterns are present. The disagreement was caused by API errors in the qwen model, not by actual security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model returned 'inconclusive' due to HTTP 400 BadRequestError when auditing .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml. These are non-critical files (neither executes during makepkg). The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 4 files and correctly identified the package as safe. The openrouter report is advisory-only (advisory: true) and doesn't count toward the verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), causing an inconclusive verdict despite these files being non-security-critical
learnings: API errors on non-critical files (like .gitignore, .nvchecker.toml) should not force an inconclusive verdict when critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, .install) are successfully audited and found safe

The audit tool should distinguish between critical files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) and non-critical files (.gitignore, editor configs, CI scripts) when determining if coverage gaps warrant an inconclusive verdict

Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be reported separately from security findings and should not automatically escalate to inconclusive when the security-critical files were successfully reviewed
